elements.label: Host hexagons regrouping into availability-zone clusters
Group-by field showing the selected availability-zone tag (dropdown closes)

sfx_review.label: music
sfx_review.note: Broadband streak lines up with the start of the regroup but matches the evenly spaced percussion train before and after it; reads as a music beat rather than a dedicated impact.

sfx_review.label: music
sfx_review.note: Continuation of the music bed, ~1 s after the burst.

pattern.description: After the group-by tag is chosen, the single sea of host hexagons breaks apart and every host travels into its availability-zone cluster, with zone headings and counts fading in; the 'From 10,000+ hosts' caption stays fixed on top.
pattern.why_premium: The data visibly reorganises itself instead of cutting to a new view, so the viewer sees that the same hosts are now grouped, and the counts land as the motion settles.

build_hint.gsap: Flip.getState('.hex'); regroup DOM into zone containers; Flip.from(state, {duration: 0.45, ease: 'power2.inOut', stagger: {amount: 0.15, from: 'random'}, absolute: true}); then gsap.from('.zone-heading, .cluster-label', {opacity: 0, duration: 0.2, stagger: 0.04}, '-=0.1'). Caption on its own static layer.
build_hint.remotion: Per hex, interpolate position from scatter layout to grouped layout with spring({frame: frame - delay_i, fps, config: {damping: 30, stiffness: 140, mass: 1}}) (no overshoot), delay_i random 0-5 frames; headings opacity interpolate(frame, [24, 30], [0, 1]).

notes: camera.move reports pull_out (scale 0.964) but the change is a content reflow of the map inside a fixed UI; no real camera move. The first filmstrip frame also shows a 'Your infrastructure' heading and an open tag dropdown that disappear at the burst start.
